category_title: Struggling emergent reader with high oral engagement but resistance to print-based skills
minimal_context: Kevin is participating in a morning meeting literacy lesson where the goal is to practice phonological awareness and sound out words on the board.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Good morning, Kevin. It's time for our morning literacy lesson. Let's look at the board and practice sounding out these words.

STUDENT: (Keeps to himself and looks away from the board) I don't want to sound them out.

TUTOR: Let's just try the first one together. What sound does this letter make?

STUDENT: (Crosses his arms and refuses to look at the letters) No.

TUTOR: Kevin, please sit up and pay attention to the lesson.

STUDENT: (Yells in a loud, angry voice) I don’t want to learn how to read! I don’t even like letters!

options.A: Take his connections to popular culture seriously by encouraging his contributions to the discussion, even if they relate to TV, movies, or video games.
options.B: Allow him to call on a neighbor, ask a friend, or poll the rest of the class for help with sounding out the words.
options.C: Terminate the instructional demands and remove the literacy materials from the board for ten seconds before attempting to resume the morning meeting lesson.
options.D: Provide the one-on-one assistance of a paraprofessional to help him sound out the words on the board during the morning meeting literacy lesson.
